| Skill rule | Baseline | Rerun |
|---|---|---|
| Newest evidence | Backup called RED from old runs; fixed later by hand | Quoted the 12:51 OK line and 13:00 gate skip; no false RED |
| Pointer check before DELETE | Missed the `/ISA` pointer | Found `WORKFLOW.md:117` (`/ISA`) and 3 `project-triage` pointers |
| Memory (agent) checked directly | Skipped (green by date) | 22 folders: 74 double index lines in 13 indexes (recounted: 74 in 13) |
| Rules diff | "No repeated correction" | 2 repeated corrections found, with session ids |
| Codex real reads | Hand-made grep | Script mode; found `fireflies-intake` read the baseline missed |
| Decision Desk step | 3 cards seeded by the main session | 7 new cards, no duplicates of the 3 open ones |

New true findings: `project-triage` skill dead since 2026-08-18; `doctor-plus` cannot be called
by the audit; `COMMANDS.md:304` Playwright path gone; `WORKFLOW.md:244` stale note;
`PFF_Position_Reports` in no router; the j-2024 paper stub; 5 Windows-era KeystoneOS notes.

## What the rerun got wrong

1. **MEMORY.md size.** It "corrected" the baseline to 1,894 chars. 1,894 is bytes; 1,865 chars
   (Python `len`) is right. `wc -m` counts bytes under a C locale.
2. **The second lost transcript.** It said "child session alone does not explain" `0c8c7095`.
   It does. Terminal (pid 69123) was started at 12:37:26 by the leaked `open -a Terminal`.
   `0c8c7095` began at 12:56 as `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` under
   `login -pf kristinarash` (the `.errors.log` callers line): a new Terminal tab, and `login -p`
   keeps the environment. Same cause, second victim. Fix: quit Terminal once.
3. **Rules scope.** 59 Codex sessions were counted, not read, so "no rule contradicted" covers
   Claude sessions only. The report says so, but the verdict line does not.
4. **Smaller.** Time-dimensioned facts checked in 1 of 22 memory folders (disclosed). The
   `project-skill-audit-2026-07` note is mostly dated history; only its "11 candidates open"
   line is stale. The stale WORKFLOW note is line 244, not 243.

Missed by both runs: `project_skill-bloat-and-promotion.md:156` records that Eric turned ArXiv,
ISA and Science back on 2026-09-13 for Codex parity, and says "retire it from canonical
instead". It supports the delete card; it is not a keep decision. (Added to the card.)

1. Measure memory caps with Python `len()` and say "chars" (stops error 1).
2. Coverage receipt per check: list what was read versus only counted, and limit each verdict to
   what was read (stops error 3).
3. One result line per DELETE: the pointer grep's live hits, its history hits read for a past
   decision, or "none" (would have caught the 09-13 note).
4. Add the repo's `docs/STATUS.md` line to the skill's write list; the rerun wrote one, as the
   repo routine requires, but the skill's read-only list does not name it.

Decision Desk card: `2026-11-02-aios-skill-fixes-2`.

A Claude session opened from inside another Claude session inherits the parent's CLAUDE_* variables and saves no transcript of its own.

**Why:** 2026-11-02: the AIOS audit session 15d95b4f was opened by the main session via open -a Terminal; Terminal was not running, so it copied the parent's environment (same CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_JOB_DIR, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION). It wrote only a subagent file, no main .jsonl, and transcript-capture.js logged 'transcript_path does not exist' 3 times. Likely also the 2026-10-23 'hidden sessions' bursts (DEV/docs/handoffs/2026-10-23-audit-followup.md), whose source was never found. Confirmed the same day: the clean-env rerun (13:03, no CLAUDE_* vars) saved its transcript (KeystoneOS 516a6136). `claude -p` with the same leaked vars still saves one (tested), so only interactive sessions are hit. ---

# /project: portfolio registry

Drives the `project-triage` CLI. The registry, `portfolio.json`, is the single
source of truth; each repo's `docs/STATUS.md` holds its tasks, which the board
reads only.

## Paths

- `$PT` is the folder holding `portfolio_json` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`.
  On the Mac that is `~/DEV/project-triage`: start each Bash call with
  `PT=~/DEV/project-triage` (the shell does not keep it between calls).
- Interpreter: `python3` on the Mac (there is no `python`). On Windows, use `python` and the
  `portfolio_json` folder from `config.windows.json` wherever this skill says `python3` and `$PT`.
- `portfolio.py` makes every change and always writes the live `$PT/portfolio.json` (only
  the read commands take `--registry`). `board.py` serves the board.

## CLI

```
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<source>"
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" add-update "<name>" "<note>" [--next-action "<step>"]
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-status "<name>" active|paused|done [--note "<note>"]
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-receiver "<name>" "<who, or me: why>"
python3 "$PT/board.py" --background
```

| Command | Prints on success |
|---|---|
| `add-idea` | `idea captured (<N> in inbox)` |
| `add-update` | `updated <name>` |
| `set-stage` | `stage set: <name> → <stage>` |
| `set-status` | `status set: <name> → <status>` |
| `set-receiver` | `<Name>: receiver <who>` |
| `board.py --background` | `board started at <url>` or `board already running at <url>` |

- Pass each name exactly as `projects[].name` spells it: `set-status` matches case-sensitively.
  Stages, in ladder order: `idea grilled spec planned building shipped`.
- `set-status active` on a row that was not active stamps `started` and renumbers the lane.
- A refused change prints `[error] <msg>` to stderr, exits 2 and leaves `portfolio.json`
  unchanged; a bad argument prints argparse usage and also exits 2. `board.py` prints
  `board did not start; see <log>` (exit 1), or a traceback when the registry fails to load.
  On any non-zero exit: stop and show the output verbatim.

## Ideas land in the board's Inbox

`add-idea` writes a card to the registry's `inbox` list, the board's Inbox column (since
2026-10-31; the older `ideas` list is history only). The card's name is `--name`, or the
pitch's first four words, made `[A-Za-z0-9_]` and suffixed `_2`, `_3` to stay unique. It
prints `idea captured as <Name> (<N> in the board inbox)`: tell Eric the card name and that
dragging it onto a lane, or `/project promote <Name>`, starts it.

## Verbs

**Name matching** (every verb that takes `<name>`): read `portfolio.json` and match the name
against `projects[].name`. One clear match: use that exact name. Several or none: ask Eric
which project before running anything.

### `idea <pitch>`
`add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<where it came from, ≤8 words>" --name <Short_Name>`, e.g.
`--source "chat about GPS vendor gaps"` (a place, not just "chat"). Pick `--name` as the
2–4 word project name the idea would get (`GPS_Vendor_Gaps`); it becomes the DEV folder name
on promotion.

### `update <name> <note>`
`add-update "<name>" "<note>"`, plus `--next-action "<step>"` when Eric gave one.

### `start` / `park` / `done <name>`
`set-status "<name>" active|paused|done`, with `--note` when Eric gave a reason. Starting a
`job`, `side` or `tool` row with no `receiver`: ask Eric who it is for, then run
`set-receiver` with his words (`me: <why>` when it is for himself).
On `start` (and after `promote`), check the project NAME for a person's name, an athlete,
a recruit or a health term (RTP, injury, women's health, DEXA...). None: run
`portfolio.py decide <name> phone-ok --source "Claude name check <date>"` so the phone page
shows it. Any, or unsure: leave it; the phone page shows "Project #n" instead.

### `stage <name> <stage>`
`set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"`. When the stage is `shipped`, offer once: "Want me to run
/harvest on <name> to distill it into your SecondBrain and log the shipped artifact?" On
yes, invoke the `harvest` skill for that project.

### `promote <idea>` and `rank`
Both change the registry where no CLI command reaches: follow
[`REGISTRY-EDITS.md`](REGISTRY-EDITS.md). Dragging cards on the board re-ranks faster.

### bare `/project`
Run `board.py --background` and give the URL. Waiting ideas are the board's Inbox column.

## After a change

The board picks up registry changes on its next poll (a few seconds); there is nothing to
render. Tell Eric in one line what changed. Closeout commits the registry as
`data: board edits <date>`, so leave `portfolio.json` uncommitted unless Eric asks.

Delete a project or idea only after Eric confirms that exact row.

**Done when:** the command printed its success line (or the hand edit saved and the
`.bak` beside `portfolio.json` was refreshed), and Eric has the one-line summary.

# Machine

Machine-specific shell, paths, and traps live in `~/.claude/machine.md` (gitignored; copy `machine.macos.md` or `machine.windows.md` to `machine.md` on a new machine). It is imported below.

@machine.md

Projects sync through GitHub (`erash11`), documents through Google Drive.

**Session routine.** When working inside a project repo, follow the Session routine in its `AGENTS.md`: `git pull` and read `docs/STATUS.md` at the start; update `STATUS.md`, commit, and `git push` at the end. This keeps the cloud sessions and any other machine in step.

# Workflow Expectations

- When asked to **create, merge, or consolidate an artifact** (calendar, deck, doc), finish with the produced file in hand. Check what exists first, then build the file even when a similar one already exists.
- **Saving, moving, or backing up a file** → read `~/.claude/STORAGE.md` first. It says where each kind of file lives.
- When the user types `/graphify`, invoke the Skill tool with `skill: "graphify"` before doing anything else.
- Skills are tools: invoke one when it clearly fits the task.
- **Decisions for Eric go on the Decision Desk** (Eric, 2026-11-02): https://claude.ai/artifact/SKUir7NZtM8NN5gwohEn3u. Seed each one with ArtifactData (2 options max, Claude's pick marked), read his clicks back from `answers`, and still list them in one line each in chat with the link. Format and fields: Tier A `feedback_decision-desk.md`. One standing page; never make a new one.
- **Writing code: climb the reuse ladder** and stop at the first rung that fully works: (1) does it need to exist at all; (2) already in this codebase, used the way the surrounding code uses it; (3) standard library or platform feature; (4) an installed dependency; (5) one line a reader gets at a glance; (6) only then, the minimum new code.
  - Read the code the change touches first, and finish every caller, test and fixture it breaks. Validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, and security stay in.
  - New logic with a branch, loop, parser, money or security leaves one small test or assert.
  - A shortcut with a known limit gets a comment: `shortcut: <the limit>, <when to upgrade>`.
  - End a coding reply with one or two lines: what was skipped or not checked, and any risk Eric must know. (Adapted from ponytail, 2026-10-20.)
- **Non-code work: decision rules** (Eric's answers, 2026-10-22):
  - Staff-facing writing: action first, clarity over polish, one page.
  - Coach reports and dashboards: open with the decision the report supports, then only the data for it.
  - Tools for staff: build on what Baylor already runs (Teams, Box, Excel, Teamworks).
  - Fast vs. thorough: thorough and checked for admin and supervisors; a small version first for coaches and Eric's own tools.
  - When Eric hands over a solution (from a video, or a named tool), restate the goal it serves, keep his idea on the table, and name a better fit if one exists before building.

# Session Startup

The `keystone-unified-snapshot.js` SessionStart hook injects `global-memory/USER.md`, `global-memory/MEMORY.md`, a summary of `transcripts/.errors.log` (only when non-empty), and a pointer to the KeystoneOS snapshot. Work from the injected copy.

- If hook failures appear, surface them once on the first response, then continue. Entries mean a hook or scheduled job failed.
- If a **"SessionStart hook could not read a required memory file"** block appears, say so on the first response.
- **If no `## User profile` block is in context at session start, the hook did not fire.** Say so, then read `USER.md`, `MEMORY.md` and `transcripts/.errors.log` by hand.
- The injection is a frozen snapshot: mid-session writes take effect next session. Load anything further only when a question needs it.

# Memory — routing only

The two-tier memory system (`~/.claude/global-memory/` and `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`) is owned by the **`memory-write` skill**, which holds the tier rules, character caps, slug rules, write steps, retrieval ladder, and daily-compiled-log rules.

The active project's Tier A memory (`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`, indexed by its `MEMORY.md`) is **auto-injected by the harness** each session. recall.py reads every Tier A folder, so they stay recallable across projects.

- Writing a fact — "remember this", "note that", "save this", "forget about" → `Skill("memory-write")`
- Recalling past context — "did we already…?", "what did we decide about X" → `Skill("memory-write")`, Recall section
- Daily compiled logs at `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/` are written only by `claude-memory-compiler`. Read one only when a question needs that day.
- **Slugs are path-based** (Mac `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-<X>`). Tier A is not auto-injected in cloud sessions or on another machine; memsearch still finds it. Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so every session sees them.

---

Maintainer note: `AGENTS.md` diverges from this file on purpose (Codex has no Skill tool, so it spells out the memory rules). Keep them as separate files; the memory procedure's one home is the `memory-write` skill.

# FOOTBALL — area index

Game film, player analytics, and the CFB prediction work.
Largest area by far: ~38,500 of the ~53,900 files in `~/DEV`.

## Projects

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `CFB_Analytics_Lab/` | CFBD API research lab. Has `MISSION.md`, `GLOSSARY.md`, `RESOURCES.md`, `learning-records/`. Largest single folder (~25k files). |
| `CFB_Victory_Model/` | Weekly prediction model. Capture cadence and rules: `/forecast-capture`, `project_cfb-forecast-capture.md`. |
| `CFB_Forecast_Archive/` | Read-only copies of the weekly forecast freezes, by year. Source of truth stays in `CFB_Victory_Model/data/`. |
| `PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026/` | Player profile build (spring 2026, TSA radar, whole-roster T-scores). Also the Perch pull host (`com.keystone.perchpull`). Successor for profiles: `Football/PerformanceSnapshot/`. Lives at the DEV root, not under `Football/`. → own `CLAUDE.md` |
| `Football/PerformanceSnapshot/` | Running player performance snapshot: VALD CMJ/IMTP + Catapult GPS + Perch 1RM, STEN vs position norms (VALD NCAA + Baylor-built), radar across Winter / Summer / In-season. Static HTML, `snapshot.py --upload` to Drive `01_PROJECTS/_STALLED/2026-10-29_PerformanceSnapshot`, rebuilt by launchd `com.keystone.snapshot` after every pull. Roster from BaylorBears.com. Read-only on the three DBs. Repo `erash11/PerformanceSnapshot`. Created 2026-10-29. |
| `PlayCalls_SuccessRate_EPA/` | 2021–2025 Baylor offensive play-call charting CSVs (PFF export) **+ the Phase 1 self-scout**, joined to PFF data (read-only) at 99.3%. Own `CLAUDE.md` + `AGENTS.md`. Private repo. Finding: success rate 57.4% → 49.5%, concentrated on 1st & 10 and the run game. **Only 2024–2025 carry outcome columns**; 2021–2023 cannot support success rate at all. Phase 1 has no EPA — that needs CFBD and is Phase 2. |
| `Game_Tracker_PWA/` | Football game tracking PWA for the coaching staff (`football-tracker-pwa/`). Own `AGENTS.md` + `docs/STATUS.md`. Git repo, pushed to erash11. Disk is the source of truth; the Claude cloud project `WebApps` is only a pointer. |
| `Practice_PlayCounts/` | Practice segment / play-count tracking PWA (`practice-tracker-pwa/`). Own `AGENTS.md` + `docs/STATUS.md`. Git repo, pushed to erash11. Disk is the source of truth; the Claude cloud project `WebApps` is only a pointer. |
| `PP_Recruiting/` | Player personnel grading: Telemetry (Teamworks) trait percentiles coupled with internal S.T.A.Q.S. grades; AGM summary build scripts. Own `AGENTS.md` + `CLAUDE.md`. Git repo, created 2026-09-14 on Windows. Finished AGM summary docs live on the primary storage drive under `02_SPORTS/Football/PP_Recruiting`. |
| `Football/` | Umbrella for 16 sub-projects, listed below. |
| `TackleAnalytics/` | Tackle analytics. Repo `erash11/TackleAnalytics`. |
| `Weekly_Matchups_2026/` | Weekly matchup analysis for 2026. Repo `erash11/Weekly_Matchups_2026`. Active on Drive `_ACTIVE`. |
| `Football_GRID/` | Football GRID work. Repo `erash11/Football_GRID`. |

## Inside `Football/`

| Sub-folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `FaceComps/` | Face-comparison work. Carries its own graph output folder. |
| `PFF_Data_Project/` | PFF data ingest and analysis. `outputs/` holds the finished reports (per-snap game demands, positional speed/collision thresholds) plus their `PROC_*.csv` working tables. |
| `CFB_Playoff_Benchmarks/` | Baylor performance tiers (bad, average, good, elite) anchored to what CFP teams actually did, plus the wins model that inverts a playoff profile into Baylor's gap. Power Four CFBD data, 2021 to 2025 reference, 2026 scored live. Own `AGENTS.md` + `docs/`. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-cfb-playoff-benchmarks-design.md`. Created 2026-10-16. |
| `MatchupAnalysis_FB2026/` | Week-by-week 2026 opponent matchup analysis. Own `CLAUDE.md` + `docs/`. Git repo. Source of truth for the project; the Claude cloud project is only a pointer to it. |
| `PlayerPersonel/` | Player personnel film review (first case: Jacorey Thomas). Python + extracted frames. Moved from `~/Documents/ChatGPT/` on 2026-09-07. Own private GitHub repo. |
| `SpeedProfiling/` | Speed profiling |
| `PlayerEvals/` | Player evaluations |
| `SpringPlayerEvals_SymAnalysis/` | Spring evals + symmetry analysis |
| `FootballBodyWeightDevelopment/` | Body weight development |
| `Baylor_Exposure_Data/` | Exposure data |
| `SP2026_03_07_ReportingROI_Football/` | Reporting ROI analysis |
| `Tezino_CampPrep/` | Camp prep |
| `football-cmj-monitoring/` | Longitudinal football CMJ pipeline (VALD ForceDecks + roster): team, position and individual views, PDF/Excel exports. Phase 0: source inventoried (`docs/SOURCE_INVENTORY.md`); reads `ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/data/forceplate.db` read-only, rep-level table `cmj_trials` built 2026-10-20 (live pull pending). Status in `docs/STATUS.md` + `AGENTS.md`. No athlete data in the repo. Created 2026-10-20. |

## Archive / dormant


## Notes

- `Football/<project>` sits at depth 2, so Keystone discovery still sees it.
  A third level would be invisible to `keystone.ps1 inventory`.
  Control plane details: see `PLATFORM.md`.
- CFBD API traps: see project memory `project_cfb-analytics-lab.md`.

## Archived 2026-10-03

Read-only on GitHub. Local copies sit in `~/DEV_archive_hold/2026-10-03/` until ~2026-11-02. Records: `project-triage/portfolio.json`.

`2025-11-25_EOS_Football_Analysis_GPS_ERR` → Coach_Report; `PostSesaonAnalysis` → Coach_Report; `CoachReport_Prototypes` → Coach_Report; `WeeklyCoachReport` → Coach_Report; `FootballWeightTargetTool` → FootballBodyWeightDevelopment; `BodWeightWeb` → FootballBodyWeightDevelopment; `2026-3-18_BodyWeightNorms` → FootballBodyWeightDevelopment; `_obsidian_extracted_from_FaceComps`; `Football_Data_DEV` → Coach_Report.

# Doctor Plus

The standard /doctor checkup, plus a workspace audit for the 6 then & now shifts from Anthropic's context-engineering article (Thariq @trq212, Jul 2026 - they cut ~80% of the Claude Code system prompt for the Claude 5 models). Read the article if a check needs the original reasoning: https://x.com/trq212/status/2080710971228918066

For a single skill, CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, review it with `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents`. This skill is the workspace-wide pass.

## Steps

1. **Re-check last time's flags.** Open the `~/DEV/docs/handoffs/*doctor-plus*.md` with the latest date in its name (file times lie: copied files are newer). For each FLAG, record FIXED, STILL, or WORSE with the evidence. Older reports there are history.
2. **Run `claude doctor`** via Bash with a 60 s timeout and summarize it. If it hangs or wants an interactive screen, note "run /doctor in your session for the built-in half" and go to step 3.
3. **Read the measured numbers.** Run the stack check and keep its context lines (`context-floor`, `skill-tax`, `memfile-*`):
   ```bash
   /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/.claude/skills/claude-stack-doctor/scripts/stack-check.ps1
   ```
   These are the always-loaded sizes for shift 3. Measure by hand only what the script does not cover (hook injections, guidance files).
4. **Map the loaded set**: guidance files (CLAUDE.md and kin), skill descriptions, rules, memory indexes, SessionStart injections. Mark each as always-loaded or on-demand. Skip version-control internals, sync backups, node_modules, caches, temp folders, and generated output.
5. **Audit each shift** (below). Judge each file against the principle the way Claude receives it; the smells are illustrations, not definitions.
6. **Write the report** to `~/DEV/docs/handoffs/YYYY-MM-DD-doctor-plus.md`: the step 1 re-check table, the `claude doctor` result, one findings table (shift, PASS or FLAG, worst offender with file and passage, suggested fix). Show it, then wait.
7. **After approval**, apply fixes one shift at a time and re-verify each. Add what changed, with commits, to the report.

**Done when** every prior FLAG has a re-check verdict, every always-loaded source has a size, every shift has PASS or FLAG citing file and passage, and the report is saved.

## The 6 shifts

1. **Judgement over rules** (then: give Claude rules). Constrain Claude only where a wrong call is costly; judgement covers the rest. Smell: absolute directives about taste or style, or two directives that pull against each other. Safety, money, deletion, approval and health-data rules are costly-if-wrong by design: leave them as they are.
2. **Interfaces over examples** (then: give Claude examples). A well-designed parameter, name, or field teaches use better than worked examples. Smell: a skill boxing Claude into worked examples where clearer parameters, names or structure would carry it.
3. **Progressive disclosure over upfront loading** (then: put it all upfront). The right context at the right time; always-loaded files earn every line. Smell: detail needed only sometimes, sitting in a file that loads every session instead of behind a pointer.
4. **One home over repetition** (then: repeat yourself). Each instruction has one authoritative home; everything else points there. Smell: the same guidance in several places, especially copies that drifted apart. Some divergence is deliberate and documented (CLAUDE.md vs AGENTS.md memory rules): check for a note before flagging.
5. **Auto-memory over guidance-file memory** (then: memory in CLAUDE.md). Facts about the user and the work (preferences, dates, decisions) belong in the memory system. Smell: dated history or decisions as prose in guidance files.
6. **Rich references over simple specs** (then: simple specs). The highest-fidelity reference wins: code, test suites, HTML mockups, rubrics. Smell: an active build steered by a markdown description where a script, test or mockup exists or is cheap to make; prose that drifted from the script it describes.

## Evidence

- Cite the file and the passage for every finding.
- A zero-hit search at root is not proof of absence: search again, narrowed, before reporting PASS.

import glob,re,os,sys,collections,shutil

    lines=open(idx).read().split('\n')
    links=[re.findall(r'\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]+\.md)\)',l) for l in lines]
    c=collections.Counter(t for L in links for _,t in L[:1])
    dups={t for t,v in c.items() if v>1}

    slug=idx.split('/projects/')[1].split('/')[0]
    shutil.copy(idx, os.path.join(B, slug+'.MEMORY.md'))

    for t in dups:
        idxs=[i for i,L in enumerate(links) if L and L[0][1]==t]
        good=[i for i in idxs if links[i][0][0].strip()!=t and links[i][0][0].strip()!=t[:-3]]
        k=(good or idxs)[0]
        drop.update(i for i in idxs if i!=k)
    new=[l for i,l in enumerate(lines) if i not in drop]
    open(idx,'w').write('\n'.join(new)); tot+=len(drop)

print('dropped',tot)
EOF

## The question that governs a skill's fate

Not "how often did I run it?" but **"would the current model do this fine
without the skill?"** If yes, the skill is a crutch that now limits the model.
Delete it. Keep only skills carrying tacit knowledge the model cannot know:
force-plate thresholds, GPS conventions, Baylor reporting norms, Eric's own
routines.

Seasonal skills (`forecast-capture`, `ingest-book`) are exempt from low-use
pressure. Judge them in season.

## Delegation contract (R2-09)

A delegate is invoked **read-only**, for a **named scope**, and its receipt is
written **only** for the scope it actually covered.

1. **Read-only.** Before invoking a delegate, instruct it explicitly: report
   findings, apply nothing, write no ledger, create no files. Several delegates
   (`improve-system` among them) begin by applying previously approved proposals
   — that must be suppressed. `aios-audit` writes only its own report, the
   `Last audited` column, and Decision Desk cards for its proposals.
2. **Scope must be verified, not assumed.** A delegate's actual coverage is what
   its body scans, not what this table wishes it scanned. `improve-system` scans
   `~/SecondBrain/` — Notes, Knowledge, Projects. It does **not** touch
   `~/.claude/projects/*/memory/` or `global-memory/`. Those are audited by
   `aios-audit` directly.
3. **A receipt covers only what was checked.** If a delegate returns findings for
   a narrower scope than its row claims, write the date **and** a scope note, or
   leave the row `unknown`. Never stamp a date because a delegate exited cleanly.

## Layout invariants the audit must assert

- `~/.claude/skills/` is canonical, is a git repo, and contains **no TRACKED symlinks**
  (`git ls-files -s` shows no mode 120000). On-disk links to third-party skills are
  expected; they are listed in the per-machine `.git/info/exclude` (never the tracked
  `.gitignore`), and a pre-commit hook refuses to commit one. What must never happen is
  committing a link, because Windows pulls this repo and a Mac link is dead there.
- `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.codex/skills/` are **generated views**. Each carries
  a `.generated-by-sync-to-codex` manifest. Every entry **in the manifest** must be
  a symlink on Mac (a copy on Windows); wrong representation is drift.
- Entries **not** in the manifest are third-party installs (`npx skills add`).
  They are counted and reported, **never** flagged as errors and never pruned.
- Support directories (`_shared/`) have no SKILL.md and must never be pruned.

## Direction of travel

**Fewer skills, stricter rules.** Skills get deleted; rules get sharpened.

## Cadence

Monthly metrics: launchd `com.keystone.aiosaudit`, day 1 at 14:00.
It writes a trend row and a nudge. It does not commit and does not push.
The agentic audit is run by hand: "audit my AI OS" in `~/DEV/KeystoneOS`.

import os,re,time,glob
now=time.time(); rows=[]
for d in ['Notes','Knowledge','Projects']:

        s=open(p,errors='ignore').read()
        m=re.match(r'---\n(.*?)\n---\n',s,re.S)
        if not m or not re.search(r'^status:\s*seed\s*$',m.group(1),re.M): continue
        age=(now-os.path.getmtime(p))/86400
        if age<=60: continue
        body=s[m.end():]; links=len(re.findall(r'\[\[',body))
        inbound=0
        rows.append((int(age),p,len(body.split()),links,re.sub(r'\s+',' ',body)[:230]))
rows.sort(reverse=True)
print(len(rows))
for r in rows: print(f"{r[0]}d | {r[1]} | {r[2]}w | {r[3]} links | {r[4]}")
EOF

import os,re,glob,time
now=time.time(); n=0
for p in glob.glob('Notes/*.md'):
    s=open(p).read()
    m=re.match(r'---\n(.*?)\n---\n',s,re.S)
    if not m or not re.search(r'^status:\s*seed\s*$',m.group(1),re.M): continue
    st=os.stat(p)
    if (now-st.st_mtime)/86400<=60: continue
    fm=re.sub(r'^status:\s*seed\s*$','status: evergreen',m.group(1),count=1,flags=re.M)
    open(p,'w').write('---\n'+fm+'\n---\n'+s[m.end():])
    os.utime(p,(st.st_atime,st.st_mtime)); n+=1
print('promoted',n)
EOF

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command for the end-of-day sequence: day log → loose ends → memory → STATUS and handoff → commit and push → one verdict.

Step 0 asks Eric one question at most. After his answer (or when Step 0 is skipped), run every
other step without pausing: invoking closeout authorizes the whole sequence. Commit and push is
standing-authorized for every DEV repo (each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine ends with it, and
unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other). On Windows or in Cowork,
read [`PLATFORMS.md`](PLATFORMS.md) for the commands that differ.

**Scope.** Every DEV repo with uncommitted or unpushed work (touched this session or not), plus
`~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory`.
A repo whose `CLAUDE.md` says its data stays local (DexaProject is the precedent) is committed,
not pushed, and listed.

**Clear to sign off when** the closing `where-was-i.py --sweep` (step 4) shows no `ACTION` line
except repos listed under "Still open" with their reason, no background job is still writing,
`.errors.log` is empty or its entries are reported, and every repo touched today has a STATUS entry
dated today with a concrete first `## Next` item, and every `card-check` gap is fixed. Questions
only Eric can answer (a receiver nobody named, a decision recorded under `## Open questions`) do
not block: `/startup` shows them tomorrow; list them under "Still open" and say "Clear to sign off".
Anything short of that: "Not clear", naming the one thing blocking.

If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and
note it. A risky fix goes under "Still open".

## Step 0 — Day log (once a day)

Closeout is the one end-of-day step Eric keeps, so it carries the two inputs the biweekly
`status-report` trusts: the supervisor log and the shipped ledger. Before 2026-10-31 they lived
only in `interview-me` and `harvest`, and both lapsed (last log 09-14, last ledger row 10-06).

`{vault_status_log}` is `vault_status_log` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`.
When `{vault_status_log}/<today>.md` or `{vault_status_log}/.asked-<today>` exists, today's log is
already taken (usually by `interview-me`): leave out the three Part 0 questions and keep only
question 4, and only when step 1 finds a candidate. No candidate and no Front Burner question
(step 2 below) as well: skip this step.

0. **Front Burner checks** (plan `project-triage/docs/plans/2026-10-31-front-burner-self-maintaining.md`):
   run `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py dates` and `... drift`. Resolve every line you
   can from evidence (STATUS dates, commits) with a cited `add-update` note. Every remaining line
   whose `needs_eric` is true (`--json`) becomes one more numbered question in step 2's batch:
   overdue step or no date → "done, new date, or no hard date?"; `off_board` → "start X?";
   `quiet` → "keep X or park it?". Ask every one, not just the first. Record answers the same day:
   one command per answer, `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py decide X <action>`:
   done → `done --step N`; new date for an overdue step → `redate --step N --date YYYY-MM-DD`;
   a date for a row that has none (`no_date`) → `redate --date YYYY-MM-DD` (no `--step`: it adds one); no hard date →
   `no-date [--step N] --reason "..." --source "..."`; an old "no hard date" still true →
   `confirm-no-date`; a row with a dated step and an old record → `drop-no-date` (no question
   needed); keep a quiet row → `keep-quiet`; "no,
   leave it off the board" → `keep-off` (stores the exact moment, so only later work is asked
   about). Start or park with `set-status`. Do not hand-edit these fields. Skipped lines are not
   blocking: list them under "Still open".

1. **Ship candidates.** Read today's dated `## Current state` lines in every repo touched today
   (the sweep in Step 1 lists them; `landed.py show --days 1` also works). A candidate is work
   handed to a person or put in use: sent, delivered, shared, presented, merged for a user, live.
   Drop any project that already has a row dated today in the ledger (`{vault_output_ledger}`).
2. **Ask once**, all at once, short answers accepted: the three Part 0 questions from
   `interview-me/SKILL.md` (that file holds their wording; left out when today's log is taken), plus:
   > 4. Did anything ship or go to someone today? I found: <candidates, or "nothing">.

   then 5, 6, ... : one per Front Burner `needs_eric` line from step 0.
3. **Write the log** (only when you asked the Part 0 questions) exactly as `interview-me` Part 0 says (output format, honest-zero rule,
   append to an existing file). On an honest zero, write the empty marker
   `{vault_status_log}/.asked-<today>` instead, so the next closeout today skips the ask.
4. **Each confirmed ship:** run the `harvest` skill for it. Eric's yes is the ship evidence harvest
   Step 1 needs; the ledger row is the required part, lesson articles only when harvest finds them.

**Done when** the log file or the marker exists for today and every confirmed ship has a ledger
row dated today.

## Step 1 — Sweep

- **Repo sweep:** `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep` (~4 s). It checks every git
  repo under `DEV/` (two levels) and the three config repos, and prints one line per repo needing
  attention; exit 1 means at least one `ACTION`. Another session, harness or machine may have left
  that work; name each such repo in the report. Flags:
  - `DIRTY`, `UNPUSHED`, `NO-UPSTREAM`, `BRANCH-AHEAD:<b>`, `BRANCH-UNPUSHED:<b>` (a local branch
    holding commits on no remote), `WORKTREE-DIRTY:<path>`: work not on GitHub. Step 4 pushes it.
  - `NOT-A-REPO`: a `.git` folder git cannot use, so the folder's work is tracked nowhere. List it;
    repair is project work, not closeout. It blocks only if this session wrote files there.
  - Info, never blocking: `STASH:<n>` (list it; leave the stash alone), `NO-REMOTE`, `DETACHED`
    (a pinned checkout), `LIVE` (session files the hooks rewrite every turn; the daily backup
    pushes them).
- **Background jobs** still running (shells, agents, workflows): wait for each to finish, or name
  it as the blocker. A job that writes after the push leaves work unpushed.
- **Registry drift:** `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is
  in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.macos.json`). It only reports. List every item under "Still
  open", any folder created this session first (a project started without a row). Fixing waits
  for a project session. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran: say so.
- Unfinished tasks from this session (TaskList), and anything promised to Eric this session and
  not delivered.

## Step 2 — Memory

Memory capture failing silently is Eric's top recurring worry; this step runs every time.

- **`~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`:** surface every entry, fix the hook issue if
  obvious, then archive and clear it as in claude-stack-doctor's `FIXES.md` → Memory pipeline
  (append to `.errors-ledger.log`, then `cp /dev/null`). The file is tracked in `global-memory`,
  so this happens before step 4's push.
- **Today's transcript** `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` exists and changed within
  the last few hours.
- **New durable decision or active thread:** update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md`
  (2,500-char cap; consolidate first) or write a Tier A memory with the `memory-write` skill.
- **Tier A stays on this machine** (its slug is built from the absolute path, which differs per
  machine). Every durable, project-scoped Tier A fact written today also goes into the repo:
  `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reason, the dated
  handoff for detail.

## Step 3 — STATUS, handoff, cards

**Handoff**, when real work happened (not just Q&A): `<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`;
workspace or system work with no single repo goes to `~/DEV/docs/handoffs/`
(`~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` is read-only history). Plain markdown that Codex,
Antigravity or a fresh Claude session can resume from:
- what was worked on and why
- decisions made, with the reasoning that would be lost
- exact paths of every file created or modified
- next actions, most important first
- anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)
- suggested skills: which ones the next session should invoke, by name

Link, don't copy: if a spec, plan, ADR, issue or commit already holds the detail, give its
path, URL or sha. Redact keys, passwords and personal data; the note is pushed to GitHub.

**`docs/STATUS.md`, in every repo touched, every time.** The next session reads it first, on

## Part 0 — Supervisor log (90 seconds, ask first)

**Three questions, asked before the reflection questions.** Facts are easier to recall
than insight when the user is tired, and a hard 90-second opener is what makes the ritual
survivable nightly. Reflection quality does not suffer from coming second; it suffers
from the user never starting.

This part exists because `status-report` — the biweekly email to the user's supervisors —
has a sourcing gap: roughly two thirds of what belongs in that email (equipment arriving,
installs, who onboarded onto what, hallway conversations, follow-ups awaiting a reply)
appears in **no** automated source. Without a nightly log, the report has to reconstruct
two weeks from memory. With one, it mostly writes itself.

`closeout` Step 0 asks these same three questions once a day. When
`{vault_status_log}/YYYY-MM-DD.md` or `{vault_status_log}/.asked-YYYY-MM-DD` exists for today,
today's log is taken: go straight to Part 0b.

> 3. Waiting on anyone, or anything about to go sideways?

`{vault_status_log}/.asked-YYYY-MM-DD` instead of a log, so `closeout` skips its ask today. A day
with no operational facts is a real day, and `status-report` trusts these entries verbatim.

# Card gaps (closeout step 3)

`portfolio.py card-check` prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either
machine, with its gaps. The live board reads each card from STATUS and the registry: a card that
makes no sense tonight makes none in six weeks (PM system design Decision 9). Fix every gap, then
re-run `card-check`.

| Gap | Fix |
|---|---|
| `STATUS has no entry dated <today>` | add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's `## Current state` |
| `STATUS has no Next item` | put one concrete action first under `## Next` |
| `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row) | set it on the board, or `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"` |
